questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes that result in property damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Closer to the truck than you would to a passenger vehicle.
Farther from the truck than you would from a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the truck than you would from a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must stay farther back from large trucks than passenger vehicles because trucks have larger blind spots.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.
At a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a red traffic light. You must always follow directions from traffic control officers, even if posted signs or signals say something different.

questions.question: This bicyclist is signaling:

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use hand and arm signals to tell other drivers what they plan to do. A left arm held straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: As daylight fades, you should use your:

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight begins to fade so others can see you. Use high beams only in open areas where no other drivers are present.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Drive to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians in a crosswalk cross first. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before you drive through.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you get tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: If you see a funeral procession, you:

options.text: Must let all vehicles in the procession go first.
May drive between the vehicles in the procession.
Must pass the procession on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let all vehicles in the procession go first.
questions.explanation: Vehicles in a funeral procession have the right-of-way. Other drivers must let all procession vehicles pass, even if you have a green light.

questions.question: A good driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead only.
Focus only on the center of the road.
Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.
questions.explanation: Watch the sides, front, and back of your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are nearby.
Yield to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. These signs alert drivers to areas where bicycles may cross the road.

questions.question: What is this symbol used for?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves at slow speeds. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: What must you do at a crosswalk?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings if they follow traffic signals. At marked or unmarked crosswalks without signals, you must stop for pedestrians.

questions.question: When is your reaction time slower?

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment and driving skills get worse. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles' movements.

questions.question: What should you do when you come up behind a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk?

options.text: May not pass that vehicle.
Should go around the vehicle if it seems safe.
May not yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not pass that vehicle.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass any vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. You must always yield to pedestrians when they enter the road.

questions.question: What should you do when turning left at an intersection?

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Park your vehicle.
You are not allowed to travel in this direction.
Exit at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are not allowed to travel in this direction.
questions.explanation: A red sign means an action is not allowed. If you see this sign, you are going the wrong way. Turn around immediately.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Relax and concentrate on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and concentrate on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, focus on driving and do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan enough time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm?

options.text: Stop.
Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, you must stop completely. Stay stopped until the signal arm retracts and the bus starts moving again. This rule applies whether the bus is ahead of you or across the street.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and constantly pass cars, what will happen?

options.text: You will reach your destination much faster and safer.
You will increase your chance of a collision.
You will help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chance of a collision.
questions.explanation: Do not pass other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a vehicle, your risk of a collision goes up.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Drive closely behind the car in front of you.
Pass the car in front of you as quickly as you can.
Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Stay farther back than normal and do not tailgate.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Drive with extra caution when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: What does tailgating (driving too close behind another car) do?

options.text: It can anger and frustrate other drivers.
It cannot result in a traffic ticket.
It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can anger and frustrate other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can lead to aggressive driving. It should always be avoided. Drivers can face legal consequences for unsafe driving.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is completely away from your vehicle's path.
Honk your horn and drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely away from your vehicle's path.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop until they are well away from your path. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.
